19.t: Working with data: an energy pyramid
q: Calculate the efficiency of energy transfer from producers to primary consumers.
Calculate the efficiency from primary to secondary consumers and compare it with question 1.
Explain why most energy is not passed on to the next level.
Most is released as heat in respiration; not every organism is eaten; indigestible parts (cellulose, bone, hair) pass out in faeces; dead material goes to decomposers.
Explain why food chains rarely have more than four or five levels.
After four transfers only about 0.1% of the producers’ energy is left: too little to support a population of top predators.

27.t: Working with data: CO₂ at Mauna Loa
q: Calculate the mean yearly rise from 1960 to 2020.
Compare the rate of rise in 1960–1970 with 2010–2020.
0.9 ppm per year in the 1960s against 2.4 ppm per year in the 2010s: the rise is speeding up.
Burning fossil fuels releases carbon fixed millions of years ago, and deforestation removes carbon sinks.
CO₂ is higher in May than in October each year. Explain.
In the northern summer, photosynthesis by forests removes more CO₂ than respiration releases, so CO₂ falls until October; in winter respiration dominates.
Suggest why Mauna Loa is a good place to measure global CO₂.
It is remote and high in the middle of an ocean, far from local sources such as cities and forests, so the air is well mixed.
